title: Align a Concealed Service Slider Using the Robot's Available Views
instruction: Adjust the orange slider in the covered service fixture until its black index aligns with the green target mark, then release it and leave it still. Keep the fixture and cover in place, avoid unintended contact with the housing or the other arm, and use only the exposed orange handle for manipulation.
context: Service technicians adjust concealed mechanisms using inspection openings while keeping a protective housing in place. This fixed task tests whether available wrist-camera views can support alignment during manipulation; no arm role or camera movement is prescribed.
setup: Original calibrated bimanual YAM station, unmodified D435 overview and D405 wrist cameras, 320x176 RGB and20 Hz controls. Coordinates in metres: x forward from the base line, y left from the base midpoint, z up; table surface z=0.7475. A rigid matte-plastic fixture is anchored to the table. Base250x200x12 mm at(0.25,0,0.7535); two150x8x8 mm rails at x0.25,y+/-0.031,z0.7675; two8x50x24 mm stops at x0.185/0.315,y0,z0.7875. An80 g orange carriage24x50x24 mm starts centred at(0.205,0,0.7875), with a rigid28x130x34 mm handle centred0.087 m toward -y and0.005 m upward from the carriage centre. It slides passively along world x for90 mm. Two8x180x108 mm end walls are centred at x0.139/0.361,y0,z0.8135; an opaque230x180x8 mm roof at(0.25,0,0.8715). Front sill214x8x12 mm at(0.25,-0.086,0.7655), header214x8x32 mm at(0.25,-0.086,0.8515). White backing150x3x18 mm at(0.25,0.026,0.8195) carries a fixed green12x1x18 mm mark at(0.270,0.0281,0.8195). A black8x1x22 mm index is fixed to the carriage at local(0,0.0256,0). The exposed handle is accessible through the -y slot; the +y opening provides an inspection view. Housing and rails remain fixed; both arms begin at the original READY pose with open grippers. All exact part transforms, colours and physical assumptions are in scene/layout.json and README.md.
scoring: Final-state score; no bonus for any arm role or camera action. Zero if at any time the fixture moves more than2 mm, slider departs the guide by more than2 mm or rotates more than2 degrees, travel leaves[-1,91] mm, or a prohibited robot contact persists for0.100 s or longer. Prohibited contacts are robot-to-fixed-fixture, inter-arm, and robot-to-slider other than finger-to-exposed-handle. Brief contacts below0.100 s do not disqualify. Within these conditions: zero while slider speed exceeds5 mm/s. Otherwise1.0 for index-to-target horizontal centre error<=8 mm, with no robot-slider contact and speed<=5 mm/s continuously for1 s;0.75 for error<=15 mm without that completed hold;0.50 for error<=25 mm;0.25 for forward displacement>=15 mm;0 otherwise. Full-score conditions terminate the trial. Force and solver-penetration values are diagnostics, not score thresholds. Missing/nonfinite evaluation data invalidates the trial rather than establishing a model score.
run_limit: 2,400 actions (120 s at 20 Hz), including 32 initial history steps; success may end early.
reset_notes: One fixed scene, seed0 and zero object jitter. Restore slider to home with zero velocity, both original READY arm poses and open grippers; clear all contact/safety/hold history. No consumables. The portable runner supports three free scripted epochs to verify reset in the same simulation process.
fidelity: Official YAM rig, cameras and controls unchanged. Task-only rigid cuboids form an anchored housing and passive 90 mm prismatic guide; friction 0.20/0.15, zero restitution. Compliance, bearing drag, wear and damage are omitted. Private 240 Hz contacts are evaluation-only; contacts under 100 ms are tolerated. Original intra-arm self-collision stays disabled; table/stand impacts are not fully monitored. An unpowered fixture analogue; full assumptions in README.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 / 2,400 actions (120 s). Scripted full-score demo: 1.0 / 280 actions (14 s), reproduced in three consecutive resets. Both use visual-contact-v2.
